answer: Reputation-weighted work routing. Each identity earns a pigment score from completed jobs, and only scores above a threshold unlock high-value assignments. Crossing the horizon into trusted tiers requires a long, verifiable task history that cannot be transferred or merged, so a clone starts at zero and must redo that labor. An attacker running many identities therefore pays the full cost of that history on each island of activity, making duplication strictly more expensive than honest work.
